paragraph: Bogota is a single-family market, plain and simple. Twenty-three sales over six months at a median of $640,000, and the housing stock is remarkably uniform: 22 of those 23 were colonials, typically three bedrooms with two full baths. No condo or co-op activity to speak of, and only a couple of multi-family closings, so there is no second tier to compare against. The sale-to-list ratio of 1.01 with 57 percent of homes going above asking and a median 21 days on market puts this in competitive but not frenzied territory. Well-priced homes move, and you should expect competition on the good ones. Sales ran from $320,000 to $750,000, so the median is the number to anchor on. The monthly counts are too thin to read a trend from, but volume clustered in spring and early summer the way it usually does here, and if Bogota follows the normal arc, expect the market to quiet into deep winter.
